name: Data Analyst
responsibilities: Query data repositories and generate the standard and custom reports that executives, managers, and clients actually review
Own the dashboards and business intelligence tools: build them, keep them updated, and support the people who depend on them
Synthesize trend data into recommendations for action, and flag industry or market shifts with strategy implications
skills: Query fluency across the data stack: database query, reporting, and business intelligence software as daily tools, not occasional ones
Interpreting the meaning of data for others: leading with what moved and why, in language a non-analyst can act on
Writing report and dashboard specifications precise enough to test the output against defined needs
Enough mathematics and economics/accounting to sanity check a metric before anyone builds a decision on it
rawSkillPool: business intelligence and data analysis software
distinctiveSkills: business intelligence and data analysis software

evidence.title: Business Intelligence Analysts (O*NET-SOC 15-2051.01), O*NET database 29.1 text release
evidence.quote: Produce financial and market intelligence by querying data repositories and generating periodic reports. Devise methods for identifying data patterns and trends in available information sources.

evidence.title: Alternate Titles for 15-2051.01, O*NET database 29.1: 'Data Analyst' is a listed alternate title for this occupation. The hinted code 15-2041.00 (Statisticians: develop or apply mathematical or statistical theory and methods) was rejected as a dishonest match for the undergrad understanding of Data Analyst.
Task statements for 15-2051.01, O*NET database 29.1
evidence.quote: Generate standard or custom reports summarizing business, financial, or economic data for review by executives, managers, clients, and other stakeholders. Maintain or update business intelligence tools, databases, dashboards, systems, or methods. Synthesize current business intelligence or trend data to support recommendations for action.
